newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Sluggish trade dampens Morocco's bourse.
newsitem.headline: Sluggish trade dampens Morocco's bourse.

text.p: Casablanca stock exchange closed on Tuesday 0.20 percent lower as blue-chip Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur slipped along with ONA group and Societe Nationale d'Investissement, brokers said.
The bourse all-share index closed at 634.32 points from 635.61 points on Tuesday.
BMCE, a market largest capitalisation, fell 18 dirhams to 582 dirhams with more than 600 shares traded.
Morocco's biggest private conglomerate, ONA dipped five dirhams to 755 dirhams, brokers said.
SNI, Morocco's second largest private group, dropped six dirhams to 720 dirhams.
Among the day's top performers were, Wafabank, which rose 10 dirhams to 790 dirhams and Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie, up five dirhams to 490 dirhams.
In the energy sector, oil refinery Samir took two dirhams to 350 dirhams. It was the biggest share of trade on the official market with more than 3,000 shares changing hands.
First and second tranche of privatisation bonds, issued in January and May 1996, remained unchanged at respectively 1,345 and 1,160 dirhams.
Steel mill Sonasid was down five dirhams to 525 dirhams.
Total traded volume on the official market was 21.6 million dirhams from 19 million dirhams, stockbrokers said.
On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 79.6 million from 26 million dirhams over the previous session.
Main trade on this market was in 47,082 Societe Cherifienne des Petroles shares.
